culturalBackground: The palm is the traditional placement for mehndi and gives the darkest stain on the body.
A round mandala in the centre of the palm, often called a tikki, is one of the oldest and best-known layouts.
Bridal designs usually cover the whole palm and continue past the wrist.
In a well-known South Asian wedding custom, the groom's name or initials are hidden in the bride's palm design for him to find.
applicationTips: Keep the palm open and relaxed until the paste dries; closing the hand smudges the centre of the design.
Start with the central motif and work outward so the layout stays symmetrical.
Palms sweat, so apply in a cool room and avoid holding anything until the paste has set.

faqPool.q: Why does mehndi stain darkest on the palm?
faqPool.a: The palm has the thickest outer skin on the hand, so it absorbs more dye and holds it longer.

faqPool.q: What is a tikki mehndi design?
faqPool.a: It is a round mandala placed in the centre of the palm, usually with decorated fingertips and the rest of the palm left bare.

faqPool.q: How long does palm mehndi last?
faqPool.a: Usually one to three weeks. Frequent hand washing and soap shorten that.
